sources.entry: Rspamd | Fast, free and open-source spam filtering system

summary.one_liner: Rspamd is an open-source spam filtering system and email processing framework that scores messages using rules, statistics, and external services.
summary.what_it_does: Evaluates each email with a set of rules including regular expressions, statistical analysis, and custom services such as URL blacklists. It returns a verdict that an MTA can act on, for example rejecting a message or adding a spam header, along with other information such as DKIM signing or suggested message modifications. Rspamd can act as a Milter to work directly with MTAs such as Postfix or Sendmail. It ships with spam filtering modules enabled by default. It exposes a Lua API for writing custom rules and plugins, and an asynchronous network API for querying DNS, HTTP, or generic TCP/UDP services. The README says it is designed to process hundreds of messages per second.
use_cases: filter spam for a mail server
reject or tag spam via Postfix or Sendmail
write custom spam rules in Lua
check URLs against blacklists in email
how_to_run: Install from Rspamd project packages for your OS (the README recommends these over distribution packages), or from FreeBSD ports, NetBSD pkgsrc, or OpenBSD ports
Follow the quick start guide in the Rspamd documentation to install and configure
notable: Acts as a Milter for Postfix and Sendmail
Comprehensive Lua API for custom rules and plugins
Asynchronous network access to DNS, HTTP, and TCP/UDP services
Built-in spam filtering modules enabled out of the box
Designed for hundreds of messages per second
caveats: README advises against distribution-packaged versions, which it says are often outdated
Full module list and configuration are in external documentation, not the README
keywords: filter spam for my mail server
